title: Five Second Talking Face Swap
tests: Tests a short video face swap with source identity, temporal consistency and original audio preserved, without misrepresenting free-tier capabilities.

faults.what: The delivered clip is 10.1 seconds long instead of the required 5 seconds.
The face replacement is not maintained throughout the delivered clip: the early samples resemble the portrait, but the samples at 6.3 and 8.9 seconds show the original woman's face again.

judge.summary: The early frames show a plausible face replacement in the original kitchen, but the clip runs twice the required length and returns to the original face.

must_haves.item: The delivered video is 5 seconds long and follows the first 5 seconds of talk-one.mp4.
must_haves.why: The supplied output duration is 10.1 seconds, not 5 seconds.

must_haves.item: The woman's face recognizably matches portrait-woman.jpg throughout, rather than reverting to the original face between frames.
must_haves.why: The face in the 1.3- and 3.8-second samples resembles the portrait, but the later samples revert to the original woman's facial features.

must_haves.item: The original kitchen, clothing, body motion and framing remain unchanged.
must_haves.why: The sampled frames preserve the kitchen layout, clothing, body placement and framing, with natural changes in hand and head pose.

must_haves.item: Original speech is audible and synchronized with the video.
must_haves.why: The sound report confirms audible speech, but a transcript and isolated frames cannot establish lip synchronization or verify that the audio is unchanged from the source.

must_haves.item: The face remains aligned during mouth and head movement, without conspicuous flicker or doubled facial features.
must_haves.why: The sampled faces appear aligned without obvious doubled features, but isolated frames cannot establish tracking stability or rule out flicker during movement.
